delta_review.summary: One documentation commit removes the production lifecycle override, expands path and secret checks, declares one seven-state/sixteen-edge lifecycle registry and paginates GitHub authority collections.
delta_review.evidence: The exact previous-to-current delta is 57 insertions and 12 deletions across three files. Every changed document and the complete 14-file base-to-head diff were reconciled; git diff --check passes.

finding_revalidation.evidence: The production override, link/inode aliases and ordinary scalar/array/object/multiline secret cases now fail, but the same semantic-governance-security fingerprint remains: nested public.vendor.api.key and JSON-escaped api_key forms receive PASS because sensitive keys are matched only in raw text.

The registry now enumerates seven statuses and sixteen edges, but it is not compatible with durable workflow authority: the production checker accepts only lifecycle state schema 1 while the canonical workflow writes schema 2, the workflow rejects the invented PlanStatusDecision type, Deferred-to-Ready reuses old plan-review authority without a recovery decision, and Ready-to-Deferred accepts the wrong source durable stage.

All GitHub authority collections use validated --paginate --slurp page sets. The stock harness passes 100/101 PR-file and review boundaries, and an independent 101-check-run variant places the required check on page two and passes the complete 143-case harness.
The refreshed 143-case harness retains and passes every cycle-two regression at the exact current head.
The refreshed 143-case harness retains and passes every original governance and error-output regression at the exact current head.

findings.title: Structured secret keys still bypass authorization-grade scanning
findings.observation: The production override and ordinary scalar, array, object and multiline secret cases now fail. The checker still classifies sensitive keys with one raw-text regular expression, without normalizing JSON escapes or deriving hierarchical structured paths. A nested public.vendor.api.key and a JSON api\u005fkey fixture both receive exit 0 and PASS.
findings.trigger: A credential is committed under an escaped sensitive key or a nested structured path such as api.key.
findings.impact: A real API key or similar credential can be committed while SECRETS and the aggregate authorization-grade result report PASS.

evidence.description: The tracked contract requires fail-closed sensitive-terminal-key scanning across scalar, array, object and multiline values.
The scanner applies one raw-text expression and does not normalize escaped keys or hierarchical key paths.
Nested and escaped-key fixtures unexpectedly pass; independent artifact SHA-256 is 772e03e2056e698bc508c0411114408e8f9b9386b2da481814637b73ff308be5.

findings.remediation: Normalize escaped structured keys before classification and parse or conservatively derive hierarchical key paths so nested api.key/database.url forms are sensitive. Keep diagnostics redacted and add both fixtures to the stock harness.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, keep all current positive cases deterministic while scalar, array, object, multiline, escaped-key and nested sensitive-path fixtures fail with redacted diagnostics.

findings.title: Lifecycle transitions remain incompatible with canonical workflow authority
findings.observation: The checker now lists all seven statuses and sixteen edges, but its authority model cannot be produced by the canonical workflow. It hard-rejects lifecycle state schema versions other than 1 while the installed workflow writes schema 2, declares PlanStatusDecision although workflowctl rejects that message type, uses old plan-review authority for Deferred-to-Ready, and validates only broad target-stage compatibility rather than the durable source stage for defer transitions.
findings.trigger: Any non-Draft projection resolves the real schema-2 state, a documented user/Requirements decision is required, Deferred-to-Ready lacks an explicit recovery decision, or a defer projection is paired with an unrelated later durable stage.
findings.impact: Valid public workflows fail while fabricated transition authority can pass. Main cannot generate checker-compatible durable evidence for the claimed lifecycle contract, and defer/recovery status can misrepresent canonical state.

evidence.description: The approved design requires seven states, sixteen guarded edges and explicit recovery for Deferred-to-Ready.
Canonical workflowctl uses state schema 2 and supports only the five Engineering Lifecycle message types, excluding PlanStatusDecision.
Changing only a valid fixture state to schema 2 makes authority validation fail; primary summary SHA-256 is 9c4540b644bdd79b31a73a750f327daa631ad0a672786ca85f5d17d6c909f78a.
Ready-to-Deferred passes with CODE_REVIEW_PENDING and Deferred-to-Ready passes without recovery authority; independent SHA-256 is 772e03e2056e698bc508c0411114408e8f9b9386b2da481814637b73ff308be5.

findings.remediation: Use the canonical schema-2 lifecycle state and only workflow-supported immutable messages, or extend and version the workflow before depending on a new decision type. Enforce exact source-stage sets per edge, require explicit recovery authority for Deferred-to-Ready, and represent every approved user/Requirements alternative.
findings.verification: Add positive end-to-end fixtures produced through workflowctl for all seven states and sixteen edges. Retain negative fixtures for schema mismatch, unsupported messages, wrong roles, wrong source/target stage, stale projection and missing recovery authority.

findings.title: Reopened Draft authority is not continuously validated
findings.observation: The checker resolves a Draft authority bundle only in the exact commit whose parent status differs. Starting from its valid Accepted-to-Draft fixture, a later Draft-to-Draft commit can replace plan and portfolio LifecycleEvidence with a nonexistent all-zero bundle, append no ChangeRecord, and still receive PASS with authoritySnapshotDigest None.
findings.trigger: After a valid Accepted-to-Draft reopen, any later same-status Draft commit tampers with or removes the supersession authority bundle.
findings.impact: The immutable proof binding the old Accepted feature and record to the reopened plan can disappear immediately after transition while deterministic evidence still reports PASS. Repository text can masquerade as current durable authority.

evidence.description: The project contract requires exact, cache-only, canonical-authority-resolved lifecycle evidence and synchronized evidence changes.
Draft authority resolution is limited to the status-changing transition commit; later Draft commits skip current and historical supersession validation.
Post-reopen all-zero evidence tampering unexpectedly returns PASS and authoritySnapshotDigest None; independent SHA-256 is 772e03e2056e698bc508c0411114408e8f9b9386b2da481814637b73ff308be5.

findings.remediation: Resolve LifecycleEvidence for every Draft with a lifecycle feature, non-None evidence, acceptance history or supersession history. Continuously bind the latest Superseded record and current Draft metadata to the exact bundle and require synchronized ChangeRecords for evidence changes.
findings.verification: Add a valid Accepted-to-Draft fixture followed by unchanged Draft and tampered Draft commits; the unchanged case must pass with canonical authority observed, while removed, nonexistent or mismatched evidence and missing ChangeRecord cases fail.
